html:
A port city on Guanabara Bay in southeast Brazil, capital of colonial Brazil, of the Portuguese empire and then of independent Brazil until 1960. Its name, "River of January", comes from Portuguese sailors who reached the bay in January 1502 and took it for a river mouth.

The Portuguese founded the city in 1565, while fighting to drive a French colony off the bay. It grew in the 1700s when gold from the interior (Brazilian gold rush) was shipped out through its port, and in 1763 it replaced Salvador as the capital. It was also the largest port of the slave trade in the Americas: hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans landed at its docks.

In 1808 the Portuguese royal family fled Napoleon and set up court here (Portuguese court to Brazil). Rio became the only European imperial capital outside Europe, and later the capital of the independent Empire of Brazil. In the 1800s coffee from the valleys inland made it rich. The writer Machado de Assis was born there in 1839.

In the 1900s Rio gave Brazil samba and bossa nova, and its carnival became world famous. The statue of Christ the Redeemer went up on Corcovado in 1931. The capital moved to Brasília in 1960, but Rio stayed Brazil's cultural face, a city of beaches, hillside favelas and huge inequality.
